decisions.statement: Status 529 matches whatever the body has.
Status 500 matches whatever the body has.
Status 502 matches whatever the body has.
Status 503 matches whatever the body has.
A matched 529 with no envelope message reads `overloaded (529)`.
A matched 500 with no envelope message reads `internal server error (500)`.
A matched 502 with no envelope message reads `bad gateway (502)`.
A matched 503 with no envelope message reads `service unavailable (503)`.
An envelope message replaces the reason the status alone would read.
The envelope error type is unread on a status this module matches by status.
Status 429 matches only an envelope naming `overloaded_error`.
A matched 429 with no envelope message reads `overloaded_error`.
A body carrying keys the envelope does not name still matches.
A status this module does not name matches nothing.
A `Retry-After` of whole seconds sets the backoff in milliseconds.
A backoff read from `Retry-After` is capped at 8000 milliseconds.
A `Retry-After` at zero or below reads the schedule instead.
A `Retry-After` the number parser refuses reads the schedule instead.
A blank `Retry-After` reads the schedule instead.
A backoff with no `Retry-After` reads the schedule at the attempt's index.
An attempt past the schedule's end reads the schedule's last entry.
An empty schedule with no `Retry-After` backs off zero.
The schedule is handed in rather than read off SERVER_ERROR_BACKOFF_MS.
Nothing here waits.
Nothing here counts the attempts a caller has made.
An envelope message that is an empty string becomes an empty reason.
An attempt below zero backs off zero rather than the schedule's first entry.
A fractional attempt backs off zero rather than a scheduled wait.
A `Retry-After` holding an HTTP date reads the schedule instead.

definition: an upstream failure a later attempt can get past
